items.title: Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2013
items.q: I could relate that experience with the making of “Take My Hand Precious Lord” by Thomas A. Dorsey, who composed that — you know it’s one of the hymns of African- American people.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you about your composition and the topics and the song titles. Most of your work looks to be allegorical or story driven, historical driven. Have you ever — I’m trying to figure out how to ask this — have you ever had music that comes to you that doesn’t have a specific intent?

Well yeah. The example is “I Feel the Thunder in My Heart” on Tiananmen. Because I was — I think I was practicing on a broken down upright piano in San Francisco Chinatown, and suddenly the thunder struck. And I could feel it through my body. And then I could relate that experience with the making of “Take My Hand Precious Lord” by Thomas A. Dorsey, who composed that — you know it’s one of the hymns of African- American people. And the story is that after his wife and child died during childbirth, he © Hamilton…

wanted to give up music, just wanted to play the blues, I think give up music in the church. And then he saw this image of the rock, I think above him, and there was like water, or tears, pouring down on the keys of the piano. And then he created the song. So I mean it wasn’t the same kind of experience, and of course in my case I wrote it was nothing like — nowhere close to the power of what he wrote. But to me that is like the music doesn’t come to me, it comes through me. And sometimes the process is like I’m…

items.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So that gives me faith and I mean people like Thomas Dorsey, stories like him, the creation of “Take my Hand Precious Lord.

ctx.x: Uh, just to wrap up, it’s September ’03 as we’re talking and how do you feel about the state of the country?

Oh well it’s like Max Roach he told me he said I can’t save the world. I mean he’s lived such a full life and you kind of see the roller coaster and the changing trends. I don’t know you know part of it is I guess being a Christian you have faith. And sometimes, well I guess the recording that David Murray and I did called “River of Life” and that’s from Revelations I think it’s 21 or 22. And I think let’s see if I can recall the scriptures, it says, “Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, as…

with I think water or tears flowing down. It’s just like the “River of Life” on the piano. I think he was trying to play some hymn, “Peace in the Valley” or something. I don’t remember. But all of a sudden this peace blossom. Take my hand precious Lord. And it’s just such a moving piece because it’s like being in sea where there’s calmness and then there’s that storm and it hits that high pitch. And I forgot where I heard Marion Williams, when I used to perform in an African-American church that was a song that…
